questions.question: Distinguish between saving and investing and give one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Saving: setting money aside safely for future use, easily accessible, mainly for emergencies and short-term goals, e.g. a savings account. Investing: putting money into assets expected to grow or produce income over a longer period, e.g. unit trusts, shares, property, retirement fund.

questions.question: Calculate the simple interest on R5 000 at 6% per year for 3 years. Explain why compound interest would give more.
questions.expected_answer: Simple interest = R5 000 × 6% × 3 = R900; total R5 900. Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus interest already earned, so each year's interest is larger (R300, R318, R337,08 = R955,08), giving more.

questions.question: What is a stokvel? Explain the relationship between risk and return and give two warning signs of an investment scam.
questions.expected_answer: A stokvel is a group whose members contribute a fixed amount regularly and receive the pool in turns or share it at a set time. Generally, the higher the possible return, the higher the risk of loss. Warning signs (any two): guaranteed very high returns; pressure to act quickly; rewards for recruiting others; vague explanations; not registered with the FSCA.
